label: unrewarded last trial, choosing a1 (D1 and D2)
explanation: Fires only at D1 and D2, never at GO and never when the reward input is 1. It needs the previous trial to be unrewarded (prev_reward==0) and the agent to be on an a1 trial, so it is a1-specific (action==2 gives almost zero). The predicate covers 99.5% of activations (mass recall 0.999), but precision is only ~0.48: about half of the unrewarded a1 D1/D2 steps stay below threshold. Activations are larger later in the episode (trials 10-89; restricting to that range gives F1 0.69), larger when S1 is the good state (good==1 holds 83% of the mass), and at D2 larger after a common transition to S1 (~0.8 of max) than a rare one to S2 (~0.2-0.4). In the examples, D1 activation grows over runs of consecutive unrewarded a1 trials. The unit does not fire after rewarded trials, on a2 trials, or at GO. At D1, action is the agent's own upcoming choice, which it can legitimately compute. The closest predicate using only observed variables, (prev_reward==0)&(prev_action==1)&(phase!=GO), scores lower (F1 0.52, mass recall 0.72). I recorded the action-based version because the agent stays on a1 after most of these trials.
